test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which special year has ISRO declared 2025 to be, highlighting its human spaceflight efforts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaganyaan Year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** Chairman, **S. Somanath**, officially declared that the **year 2025** will be celebrated as the **"Year of Gaganyaan"**. This declaration underscores India’s commitment to its maiden human spaceflight mission. ***Hence, the option Gaganyaan Year is correct.***
 
• The primary objective of **2025** is to conduct a series of critical test flights and preparatory missions to ensure the safety and success of the eventual crewed mission. These include the **G1**, **G2**, and **G3** missions, which are uncrewed flights designed to test the orbital module and recovery systems.
 
• The **Gaganyaan** mission aims to demonstrate human spaceflight capability by launching a crew of **three members** to an orbit of **400 km** for a **3-day mission** and bringing them back safely to earth, landing in Indian sea waters.
 
• The declaration of **2025** as a dedicated year for this project highlights the transition from the design and experimental phase to the actual execution phase of the **Human Spaceflight Centre (HSFC)**.
 
• The **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**, has been identified as the launch vehicle for the mission, specifically reconfigured to meet human-rating requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Astronaut Selection and Training:** Four designated test pilots from the **Indian Air Force (IAF)**—Group Captain **Prashanth Nair**, Group Captain **Ajit Krishnan**, Group Captain **Angad Pratap**, and Wing Commander **Shubhanshu Shukla**—have been selected for the mission. They underwent extensive training at the **Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center** in **Russia** and are currently training at **ISRO’s** facilities in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Mars Year:** While **ISRO** achieved global fame with the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)** or **Mangalyaan** in **2014**, 2025 is not designated as Mars Year. Future plans include **Mangalyaan-2**, but the immediate priority remains human spaceflight. ***Hence, the option Mars Year is incorrect.***
 
• **Solar Year:** This would typically refer to missions like **Aditya-L1**, India's first solar observatory launched in **September 2023**. While **2024** saw significant data collection from **Aditya-L1**, **2025** is specifically branded for the human mission. ***Hence, the option Solar Year is incorrect.***
 
• **Moon Year:** Following the historic success of **Chandrayaan-3** in **August 2023**, India became the first country to land near the **Lunar South Pole**. Future lunar missions like **LUPEX** (with **JAXA**) and **Chandrayaan-4** (sample return) are planned, but 2025 is not designated as Moon Year. ***Hence, the option Moon Year is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vyommitra:** To ensure the safety of human astronauts, **ISRO** will first launch a female robot humanoid named **Vyommitra** in the uncrewed missions (specifically **G1**). This humanoid is designed to simulate human functions in the space environment and monitor life support systems.
 
• **Budget and Infrastructure:** The **Union Cabinet** initially approved a budget of approximately **₹9,023 Crore** for the **Gaganyaan** programme. Infrastructure like the **Crew Escape System (CES)** and the **Service Module** have undergone rigorous testing, including the **TV-D1** (Test Vehicle Abort Mission-1) conducted in **October 2023**.
 
• **Global Context:** If successful, **India** will become the **fourth nation** in the world to launch a crewed spaceflight mission, following the **USA**, **Russia (Soviet Union)**, and **China**. This achievement will be a major milestone for the **Department of Space** and the **Indian government’s** vision for an **Atmanirbhar Bharat** in high-end technology.
 
• **Axiom-4 Mission:** As a precursor to the main mission, **India** is collaborating with **NASA** to send one of its selected astronauts (**Shubhanshu Shukla**) to the **International Space Station (ISS)** via the **Axiom-4** mission scheduled for late **2024** or early **2025**.
